value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation, Australian Taxation Office Client Register
variable_description: Whether the ATO still trusts the address on this row, which turns unreliable once post sent to it comes back undelivered. The register itself is the ATO's roll of people with a tax file number, which ABS describes as "demographic data about individuals who require a tax file number to interact with government, business, financial, educational and other community institutions". Read it with ADDR_STS_CD, which says whether the address is the current one, and with the SA1, SA2, SA4 and state columns, which are this address geocoded.
value_definition: A two-state indicator. The data item list names reliable and unreliable as the outcomes but publishes no codes, so the stored characters are not confirmed.
limitation: It grades the ATO's postal experience, not the person's whereabouts. An address can be perfectly current and still be flagged unreliable because a letterbox or a business tenancy failed, and nothing here dates the returned item, so an unreliable flag cannot be placed in time against the address episode it sits on.
rationale: No ATO or ABS page publishes the codes for this field. The custodian's own wording states the rule that sets it, and the ABS PLIDA page establishes what the client register is and who is on it, which is what the description asserts.
evidence_quote: Client Register, from 2006: demographic data about individuals who require a tax file number to interact with government, business, financial, educational and other community institutions
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's parenthetical wording as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so it never said that the flag is about returned post rather than about whether the person has moved.

value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation, Australian Taxation Office Client Register
variable_description: Whether the ATO still holds this address as one it would use for the client, or has superseded it. It is the column that separates a client's current address from the trail of earlier ones, so a person-year address panel built without filtering on it will hold several addresses for the same day. START_DATE and END_DATE date the episode; this column reports the state of the record as at the extract.
value_definition: A short status code. The data item list names active and inactive as the outcomes and publishes no code characters, so the stored values are not confirmed.
limitation: Inactive is not the same as wrong. A correct historical address is inactive the moment the client notifies a new one, and because the status is assessed at extraction, a row that was the client's live address in 2012 reads inactive in a 2022 extract. It also says nothing about whether post to the address arrives, which is ADDR_RELIABLE_STS.
rationale: No published ATO page enumerates the codes. The custodian's wording gives the two outcomes, and the ABS PLIDA page establishes the register as the ATO's demographic roll of tax file number holders, which is what makes the active or inactive distinction an administrative currency flag.
evidence_quote: Client Register, from 2006: demographic data about individuals who require a tax file number to interact with government, business, financial, educational and other community institutions
supersedes_rationale: The entry reused the custodian's bracketed wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence in both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing warned that an address panel needs this column to avoid stacking superseded addresses on the same day.

value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation, Australian Taxation Office Client Register
variable_description: The 2025 vintage spelling of the column saying whether this address is where the client lives or where the ATO posts their mail. The 1999 to 2022, 2023 and 2024 address tables carry the same field as ADR_TYP, so code that stacks the vintages has to accept both names or it silently drops the type on the newest table. POSTALTYPE beside it sub-classifies a postal address into a box, bag or roadside service.
value_definition: A short type code. The data item list gives postal and residential as its examples and publishes no code characters, so the stored values are not confirmed.
limitation: The rename is the trap rather than the concept: a series joined on variable name alone loses the 2025 table, and there is no published statement that ADDR_TYP and ADR_TYP use the same codes, so the two cannot be assumed to be interchangeable without checking. A client with only a postal address on file has no residential row at all.
rationale: The registry shows this name only on ato_cr_addr_1999_25 while ADR_TYP appears on the four earlier address tables, which identifies it as the renamed field; the ABS PLIDA page establishes the register the field sits in.
evidence_quote: Client Register, from 2006: demographic data about individuals who require a tax file number to interact with government, business, financial, educational and other community institutions
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, and said nothing about the rename that makes the 2025 table look as though it lost the field.

value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation, Australian Taxation Office Client Register
variable_description: The standing the ATO gives this person as a client of the tax system, on the demographic side of the client register. It sits with START_DATE and END_DATE, so the register carries a history of statuses rather than one current value, and a person can appear several times with different codes. ABS describes the register as "demographic data about individuals who require a tax file number", which is the population the status applies to.
value_definition: A short administrative code with no published list. The register's own metadata does not name the outcomes, so both the code characters and the number of distinct statuses are unconfirmed.
limitation: A client status is a state of the ATO's record, not a statement about the person's tax affairs. It cannot be read as employed, resident, lodging or earning, and an inactive client can still have income reported about them by a third party through payment summaries or Single Touch Payroll.
rationale: No ATO or ABS publication enumerates client register status codes. The ABS PLIDA page defines the register and its population, which supports the description of what the status attaches to, but not the values.
evidence_quote: Client Register, from 2006: demographic data about individuals who require a tax file number to interact with government, business, financial, educational and other community institutions
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed only the custodian's typo, 'Client staus code', with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so a reader learnt neither what the status attaches to nor that it is dated rather than current.

value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation, Department of Home Affairs Client information
variable_description: A flag saying the person on this ATO client record also appears in the immigration department's client data. The prefix is the Department of Immigration and Citizenship, the name Home Affairs used before 2013, and the PLIDA source it points at holds "Client information on Australian-born citizens, temporary & permanent migrants", from 1984. It is a coverage flag on the ATO record, not an attribute of the person, so it changes as the immigration extract is refreshed.
value_definition: A binary indicator on the demographics record. The register's metadata does not publish the characters used for present and absent.
limitation: It is not a migrant marker. The immigration client file covers Australian-born citizens as well as visa holders, so a positive flag does not mean overseas born, and a negative flag mixes people genuinely absent from immigration data with people whose records did not match. Nothing here gives a visa, a country or an arrival date.
rationale: The ABS PLIDA page names the Home Affairs Client information dataset that this flag points at and states its population, which is the fact that decides whether the flag can be read as a migrant indicator.
evidence_quote: Client information on Australian-born citizens, temporary & permanent migrants.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's sentence about presence in immigration data and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader would reasonably have used it as a migrant flag.

value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation, Australian Taxation Office Client Register
variable_description: The client's birth month and year as the ATO holds them, with the day removed before the file reached the asset. It is the only age information on the ATO client register, so an age at any dated event has to be built from it rather than read off a column. The register is the ATO's roll of tax file number holders, so the date is what was given at registration, not a date verified against a birth record.
value_definition: A character string pairing a three-letter month with a four-digit year, in the form Mar1978. It is not a date type, so it needs parsing before any arithmetic.
limitation: Dropping the day makes every age uncertain by up to a month, which matters at policy boundaries such as turning 18, 60 or the age pension age within a quarter. The value is also self-reported at registration and can be a default rather than a true birth date, so it should not be treated as vital-registration quality.
rationale: The custodian states the format, and the ABS PLIDA page establishes that the register is the ATO's tax file number client roll, which is what makes the date a registration-time value rather than a verified one.
evidence_quote: Client Register, from 2006: demographic data about individuals who require a tax file number to interact with government, business, financial, educational and other community institutions
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave only the format string and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said that this is the register's only age information or that the missing day limits age precision.

value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation, Australian Taxation Office Client Register
variable_description: The day the record on this row stopped applying, which is what turns the client register into a history rather than a snapshot. On an address row it closes an address episode; on a demographics row it closes a version of the client's details, so the same column name carries two different subjects across the nine tables it appears on. Pair it with START_DATE to build non-overlapping episodes.
value_definition: A calendar date. Rows still current at extraction carry either a missing value or a far-future sentinel, so the open end of an episode has to be handled before any duration is calculated.
limitation: It dates the ATO's record, not the person's life. An address episode ends when the client tells the ATO or the ATO updates the record, which can be months after the move, and a demographics episode can close simply because an unrelated field on the record was corrected.
rationale: The custodian publishes no more than the words 'End date'. The registry shows the column on both the address and demographics tables, which establishes the two subjects, and the ABS PLIDA page establishes the register itself.
evidence_quote: Client Register, from 2006: demographic data about individuals who require a tax file number to interact with government, business, financial, educational and other community institutions
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the two words 'End date' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say what ends, that the subject differs between the address and demographics tables, or that open episodes need handling.

value_source: ABS, Statistical Spatial Framework guidance material, Geocoding unit record data using address and location
variable_description: How well the client's address matched the ABS address index when it was coded to geography, and so how much weight the SA1 on the same row can carry. ABS defines the underlying step as "the process of matching a reported address against an index of geocoded addresses to obtain the geocode for the reported address", and recommends keeping the match outcome alongside the geocode for exactly this reason. SUB_ADR_FLAG carries the second, finer level of the same assessment.
value_definition: A short coding outcome flag written by the ABS address coding run, not by the ATO. Neither the ABS nor the data item list publishes the characters, so the number of levels is unknown.
limitation: A good match flag certifies the match, not the address. An address keyed accurately from a stale ATO record codes cleanly to the wrong suburb, and the flag will not show it. Because the flag has no published levels, it cannot be turned into a quality threshold without first tabulating it in the data.
rationale: The field sits with SUB_ADR_FLAG, the IN_MAY indicators and the ASGS geography columns, which is the signature of an ABS address coding run; the SSF guidance defines the step and recommends retaining match information with the geocode.
evidence_quote: Address geocoding is the process of matching a reported address against an index of geocoded addresses to obtain the geocode for the reported address.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Address coding flag' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so a reader could not tell that it grades a match rather than an address.

value_source: ABS, Statistical Spatial Framework guidance material, Geocoding unit record data using address and location
variable_description: Says whether this address was coded in the May 2022 run of the ABS address index, and it appears only on the 1999 to 2022 vintage of the address table. Each vintage of the table carries its own indicator, so a row's geography comes from the run its own flag names. ABS describes coding as "matching a reported address against an index of geocoded addresses", and the index is rebuilt between runs, which is why the vintage is recorded at all.
value_definition: A yes or no indicator for the May 2022 coding run. The data item list does not publish the characters used, so whether it is stored as Y and N or as 1 and 0 has to be read off the data.
limitation: A negative value does not mean the address was never coded. It means this run did not code it, so the SA1, SA2, SA4 and state values on the row came from a different run and are not guaranteed comparable with rows the May 2022 run did code.
rationale: The custodian's wording names the coding run and the index, and the ABS SSF guidance defines what an address index and a coding run are; the registry confirms the flag appears only on the 2022 extract table.
evidence_quote: Address geocoding is the process of matching a reported address against an index of geocoded addresses to obtain the geocode for the reported address.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's sentence and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say that a negative value points at a different coding run rather than at missing geography.

value_source: ABS, Statistical Spatial Framework guidance material, Geocoding unit record data using address and location
variable_description: The address index vintage flag on the 1999 to 2023 address table, one year on from IN_MAY_22. The custodian's own wording for it still reads May 2022, which is a carried-over sentence rather than a statement that the 2023 table was coded to the older index. Treat the variable name as the authority on the run and the description as unreliable on this one point.
value_definition: A yes or no indicator for the May 2023 coding run, carried alone on the 1999 to 2023 address table. Its characters are unpublished, and its custodian sentence names a different run from its name.
limitation: The mismatch between the name and the custodian's sentence means the run cannot be confirmed from the metadata alone, so a study that needs to know exactly which index produced a row's SA1 has to confirm it with the ABS rather than read it here.
rationale: The registry shows this flag only on ato_cr_addr_1999_23 while the identically shaped IN_MAY_22 and IN_MAY_24 sit on their own vintages, which identifies the pattern; the ABS SSF guidance supplies the concept of an address index run.
evidence_quote: Address geocoding is the process of matching a reported address against an index of geocoded addresses to obtain the geocode for the reported address.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's May 2022 wording on a variable named for 2023, with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it propagated the inconsistency instead of flagging it.

value_source: ABS, Statistical Spatial Framework guidance material, Geocoding unit record data using address and location
variable_description: The May 2024 address index flag, and the only one of the four that appears on two tables: the 1999 to 2024 address table and its v2 reissue. Both tables therefore describe the same coding run, so a row present in each is not two coding events. ABS describes the step as "matching a reported address against an index of geocoded addresses", which the flag dates.
value_definition: A yes or no indicator for the May 2024 coding run, carried identically on the original 2024 address table and its reissue. The characters used are not published.
limitation: Because the flag spans the original and the reissued 2024 table, it cannot tell you which of the two you are reading, and stacking both without deduplicating will double a person's address episodes. It also says nothing about why the table was reissued.
rationale: The registry shows this flag on both ato_cr_addr_1999_24 and ato_cr_addr_1999_24_v2, which is the fact that distinguishes it from the other three; the ABS SSF guidance supplies the coding-run concept.
evidence_quote: Address geocoding is the process of matching a reported address against an index of geocoded addresses to obtain the geocode for the reported address.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's sentence with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not mention that the same flag sits on a reissued table where naive stacking duplicates rows.

value_source: ABS, Statistical Spatial Framework guidance material, Geocoding unit record data using address and location
variable_description: The May 2025 address index flag, on the newest address table, which is also the first to carry a mesh block and a hashed address register identifier. Those two additions are the practical reason to care about the run: MB_ASGS_2021 and ARID_HASH_TRUNC exist only where this coding run reached, so the flag bounds what the finest geography on the register covers.
value_definition: A yes or no indicator for the May 2025 coding run, the run that first brought mesh block geography onto the register. The characters used are not published.
limitation: It does not certify that the mesh block on the row is present, only that the row belongs to the 2025 run, so an address can sit inside the run and still have no mesh block if the match failed. Comparing 2025 geography with a 2022 or 2023 table compares two index builds, not two locations.
rationale: The registry shows this flag only on ato_cr_addr_1999_25, the same table that first carries MB_ASGS_2021 and ARID_HASH_TRUNC; the ABS SSF guidance supplies the address index and coding-run concept.
evidence_quote: Address geocoding is the process of matching a reported address against an index of geocoded addresses to obtain the geocode for the reported address.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's sentence with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, and did not connect the run to the new mesh block and address identifier columns that arrive with it.

value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, July 2021 - June 2026, Mesh Blocks
variable_description: The finest geography on the ATO client register, giving the block of roughly 30 to 60 dwellings the client's address falls in. ABS defines them as "the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS", which "form the building blocks for the larger regions of the Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS)", and there are 368,286 of them. It arrives only with the 2025 vintage of the address table, so mesh block geography is not available on the 2022, 2023 or 2024 extracts.
value_definition: An eleven-digit ASGS Edition 3 mesh block code. The 368,286 codes include 114 non-spatial special purpose codes for people in transit or with no fixed address, which are valid values rather than errors.
limitation: A mesh block is not a household or a neighbourhood. ABS designs them around land use, so a block can be entirely commercial or a park, and two people in the same block are not co-resident. Because the column exists only on the 2025 table, any mesh block time series across ATO client register vintages has to be rebuilt from SA1 instead.
rationale: The custodian names the column as a mesh block coded to the 2021 ASGS, and the ABS ASGS Edition 3 page defines mesh blocks, gives their count and design and names the special purpose codes a user will meet in the data.
evidence_quote: Mesh Blocks are the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS and form the building blocks for the larger regions of the Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS).
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Mesh block coded to 2021 asgs' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it gave neither the size of a mesh block, the special purpose codes, nor the fact that only one of the five address tables has it.

value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, July 2021 - June 2026, Statistical Area Level 1
variable_description: The small area of about 400 people that the client's address falls in, and the finest geography available on every vintage of the address table. ABS defines SA1s as "geographic areas built from whole Mesh Blocks" and designs them to hold 200 to 800 people. Because ATO_CR carries SA1, SA2, SA4 and state but no SA3, an SA3 analysis has to be built up from this column through an ASGS correspondence.
value_definition: An eleven-digit ASGS Edition 3 SA1 code. There are 61,845 of them, including 34 non-spatial special purpose codes for people in transit or with no fixed address.
limitation: An SA1 of 400 people is small enough that a count of taxpayers in one can be disclosive, and small enough that the address coding match quality carried in FLAG decides whether the code is right. Its 2021 boundaries are also applied to addresses held from 1999, so an SA1 in an early episode is a modern area containing an old address, not the area as it existed then.
rationale: The custodian names the column as the SA1 location, and the ABS ASGS Edition 3 page defines SA1s, gives their population design range and their count including the special purpose codes.
evidence_quote: Statistical Areas Level 1 (SA1s) are geographic areas built from whole Mesh Blocks.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Sa1 location' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it gave no sense of the size of an SA1, the special purpose codes, or the absence of SA3 from this register.

value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, July 2021 - June 2026, Statistical Area Level 2
variable_description: The suburb-scale community the client's address falls in, and the level most ABS non-Census statistics are published at. ABS defines SA2s as "medium-sized general purpose areas built up from whole Statistical Areas Level 1 (SA1s)" whose "purpose is to represent a community that interacts together socially and economically", generally holding 3,000 to 25,000 people. It is the level at which an ATO client register count can usually be compared with published population or income estimates without a correspondence.
value_definition: A nine-digit ASGS Edition 3 SA2 code. There are 2,473 of them, including 19 non-spatial special purpose codes such as Migratory - Offshore - Shipping and No Usual Address.
limitation: An SA2 is a community, not a labour market or a service catchment, so it should not be used to define where someone works. It is also not nested inside the SA4 on the same row in any way a user needs to construct: both were assigned by the same coding run, so a mismatch between them signals a coding problem rather than a person straddling areas.
rationale: The custodian names the column as the SA2 location, and the ABS ASGS Edition 3 page defines SA2s, states their purpose, gives their population range and lists the special purpose codes.
evidence_quote: Statistical Areas Level 2 (SA2s) are medium-sized general purpose areas built up from whole Statistical Areas Level 1 (SA1s). Their purpose is to represent a community that interacts together socially and economically.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Sa2 location' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not say what an SA2 represents or why it is the natural level for comparison with published ABS statistics.

value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, July 2021 - June 2026, Statistical Area Level 4
variable_description: The labour market region the client's address falls in, and the coarsest geography on the register below state. ABS defines SA4s as "geographic areas built from whole Statistical Areas Level 3 (SA3s)" and states that "SA4 boundaries represent labour markets and the functional area of Australian capital cities respectively". That makes it the right level for reading ATO client counts against Labour Force estimates, which are published on the same regions.
value_definition: A three-digit ASGS Edition 3 SA4 code. There are 108 of them, including 19 non-spatial special purpose codes, and the four Other Territories share a single SA4.
limitation: An SA4 is where a person lives, not where they work, even though the boundaries were drawn around labour markets. ABS also designs SA4s for stability rather than homogeneity, so a regional SA4 of 100,000 to 300,000 people can span a capital city fringe and its hinterland, and an average taken over one hides that spread.
rationale: The custodian names the column as the SA4 location, and the ABS ASGS Edition 3 page defines SA4s, states the labour market purpose that makes the level meaningful and gives the count and the Other Territories treatment.
evidence_quote: Statistical Area Level 4 (SA4s) are geographic areas built from whole Statistical Areas Level 3 (SA3s). SA4s are the largest sub-state regions in the Main Structure of the ASGS and are designed for the output of a variety of regional data, including data from the 2021 Census of Population and Housing.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Sa4 location' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it never said that SA4s are labour market regions or that they are the level Labour Force statistics use.

value_domain: Sex as recorded on the ATO client register
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation, Australian Taxation Office Client Register
variable_description: The client's sex as the ATO holds it, taken from what was given when the tax file number was registered rather than from a birth or death record. It sits on the dated demographics record with START_DATE and END_DATE, so a change is a new episode rather than an overwrite and the register can show a person's recorded sex changing over time. ABS describes the register as "demographic data about individuals who require a tax file number".
value_definition: A short sex code with no published list. The number of categories is unconfirmed, so whether the register carries anything beyond male and female cannot be read from the metadata.
limitation: It is an administrative attribute of a tax record, not a measured characteristic, and it is not collected to an ABS standard, so it should not be pooled with Census or vital statistics sex without checking that the categories agree. Where the value differs from a linked Census or birth record, this column is not the authority.
rationale: No ATO or ABS publication gives the client register's sex categories. The ABS PLIDA page establishes the register as the ATO's demographic roll of tax file number holders, which supports the claim that the value comes from registration.
evidence_quote: Client Register, from 2006: demographic data about individuals who require a tax file number to interact with government, business, financial, educational and other community institutions
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the single word 'Sex' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it gave neither the source of the value nor the fact that it is a dated episode that can change.

value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation, Australian Taxation Office Client Register
variable_description: The day the record on this row began to apply, and the column that lets a client's address or demographic history be cut at any date. On an address row it opens an address episode; on a demographics row it opens a version of the client's details, so its subject differs between the address and demographics tables even though the name does not. The earliest dates run back to 1999, well before the 2006 start ABS gives for the register in PLIDA.
value_definition: A calendar date. Episodes are intended to be contiguous within a client, so a gap between one END_DATE and the next START_DATE is a period with no record rather than a period living nowhere.
limitation: It records when the ATO began using the record, not when the change happened. A person who moved in March and told the ATO in October gets an October start, so durations built from this column measure notification lags as well as residence, and comparing it against a Census night address will show apparent moves that are only reporting delays.
rationale: The custodian publishes only the words 'Start date'. The registry shows the column on both the address and demographics tables and the table names run from 1999, while the ABS PLIDA page dates the register from 2006, which is the discrepancy a user needs flagged.
evidence_quote: Client Register, from 2006: demographic data about individuals who require a tax file number to interact with government, business, financial, educational and other community institutions
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the two words 'Start date' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it said neither what starts nor that the date is a notification date rather than an event date.

value_domain: ASGS 2021 State and Territory code (1 to 9)
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, July 2021 - June 2026, Australia and State/Territory
variable_description: The state or territory the client's address falls in, held as an ASGS number rather than an abbreviation. ABS codes them 1 New South Wales through 8 Australian Capital Territory, with 9 Other Territories covering Jervis Bay, Christmas Island, the Cocos (Keeling) Islands and Norfolk Island together. It is derived from the same address coding run as the SA1, SA2 and SA4 on the row, and ABS warns that these are "a cartographic representation of legally designated boundaries and therefore should not be used for legal purposes".
value_definition: A single digit from 1 to 9 under ASGS Edition 3. Code 9 is a grouping of four separate territories rather than one place, and the non-spatial special purpose codes for people in transit or with no fixed address also resolve to a state value.
limitation: It is not the taxpayer's state of residence for tax or transfer purposes, which turns on where a person actually lives rather than on the address the ATO last recorded. A client whose row holds a postal address takes their tax agent's state, so the address type column, ADDR_TYP on the 2025 table and ADR_TYP on the earlier ones, has to be checked before the column is read as where someone lives.
rationale: The custodian describes the column as a state number, and the ABS ASGS Edition 3 page publishes the one-digit code list in full and states the caution about legal use.
evidence_quote: The ASGS State and Territory boundaries are a cartographic representation of legally designated boundaries and therefore should not be used for legal purposes.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'State (number)' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it neither gave the nine codes nor said that code 9 groups four territories.

value_source: ABS, Statistical Spatial Framework guidance material, Geocoding unit record data using address and location
variable_description: The second level of the address coding assessment, qualifying the outcome that FLAG summarises. It matters most for addresses with sub-dwellings, where a unit in a block may code to the building rather than to the unit, and the ABS guidance asks that the degree to which a reported address matched the index record be kept with the geocode. Read the two flags together: FLAG says which outcome, this says how exact.
value_definition: A short secondary coding flag written by the ABS address coding run. Neither the ABS nor the data item list publishes its levels, so it can only be characterised by tabulating it in the data.
limitation: It cannot be read on its own, because the same sub-flag value can qualify different FLAG outcomes. It also does not say what was imprecise: a unit coded to its building and an address coded to a nearby locality centroid are both imprecise, and only one of them will put the person in a different SA1.
rationale: The field name and its position beside FLAG and the ASGS columns identify it as a secondary outcome of the ABS address coding run; the SSF guidance sets out the recommendation to retain match detail, but publishes no levels for this field.
evidence_quote: Address geocoding is the process of matching a reported address against an index of geocoded addresses to obtain the geocode for the reported address.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Address coding sub flag' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it did not say what the flag qualifies or that it is meaningless without FLAG.

value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation, Australian Taxation Office Client Register
variable_description: The person key that joins the client register's address history to its demographics and to the rest of PLIDA. It is the reason the register is useful at all: on its own it holds no income, but as the ATO's roll of everyone with a tax file number it supplies a denominator that tax returns and payment summaries can be counted against. ABS describes the register as "demographic data about individuals who require a tax file number to interact with government, business, financial, educational and other community institutions".
value_definition: A synthetic linkage identifier, held as a character string, with no meaning in its characters. It is not a tax file number, an ATO client identifier or an ABN, so it can be matched across products but not decoded.
limitation: It identifies a person only where the ATO record linked to the person spine, so a client who did not link is missing rather than absent from the tax system. Having a key here is also not evidence of tax activity: needing a tax file number for a bank account or a student loan puts someone on the register without any return, and a register-based denominator will therefore differ from a lodger-based one.
rationale: The ABS PLIDA page names the client register among the ATO datasets held as enduring linkages and states what its population is, which is what makes this key a denominator rather than a sample of taxpayers.
evidence_quote: Client Register, from 2006: demographic data about individuals who require a tax file number to interact with government, business, financial, educational and other community institutions
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Synthetic MADIP Person ID' on the demographics tables and 'Synthetic person level identifier for ATO datasets' on the address tables with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it never said that the register is a whole-population roll rather than a file of lodgers.
